rough_goal: Automate my @crispykitchen TikTok reels operating system end to end -- ideate from cooking trends, produce short videos, post on a cadence, and double down on what performs

answers.success_criteria: Success is a self-running reel pipeline for @crispykitchen that ships at least 2 finished reels per day and sustains a 14-reel weekly backlog, lifting average 48-hour view-through from about 18% to at least 28% and follower growth from about 1,200 to at least 4,000 net new followers per month, verified in TikTok Analytics and Buffer. Every published reel must carry a Buffer schedule record and a logged 48-hour performance snapshot, and at least one owner-approved theme must show a measurable before/after engagement lift each week.
answers.subject_scope: The work is about short-form cooking reels for the @crispykitchen TikTok account, the trend themes sourced from TikTok Creative Center and cooking hashtags, the individual reel assets produced in CapCut from approved stock B-roll and original footage, the Buffer scheduling queue, the TikTok publishing endpoint, and the per-reel performance metrics (views, watch-through, saves, shares) tracked over a 48-hour window.
answers.allowed_context: Hermes may read TikTok Analytics and Buffer reports, pull trend signals from TikTok Creative Center, draft scripts, storyboards, captions, and hashtag sets, and assemble reels in CapCut using only approved stock B-roll libraries and the owner's own footage. Read-only research and drafting are preferred. No music outside the licensed library, no personal accounts, and no live posting without an approved schedule are allowed.
answers.approval_boundaries: Owner approval is required before creating any Buffer schedule entry, before publishing any reel to TikTok, and before using any new music or stock source not already on the approved list. Hermes must never post more than the configured daily reel target, never use copyrighted audio, never publish food-safety or health claims without review, and never spend on paid promotion. Ideation, scripting, and CapCut production are autonomous; every external send (Buffer schedule, TikTok publish) is owner-approval-gated and TikTok publishing is irreversible.
answers.workflow_path: First ideate trend themes from TikTok Creative Center and cooking hashtags, then draft the script, storyboard, caption, and hashtag set, next produce the reel in CapCut from approved B-roll, then route it to owner review or auto-clear it when it matches an approved theme, after that create the Buffer schedule entry and publish to TikTok on the daily cadence, then watch performance for 48 hours, and finally double down on winning themes or cut underperformers. Stop when the daily reel target is met, when the backlog is exhausted, when owner approval is withheld, or when a hard stop like an irreversible publish without approval would be breached.
answers.proof_requirements: Every published reel needs a Buffer schedule record, a TikTok publish confirmation, and a 48-hour performance snapshot with views, watch-through, saves, and shares logged to the reel card. Each week needs a theme scorecard ranking double-down versus cut decisions, an approval audit log of every owner-gated publish, and a compliance check confirming licensed audio only and no unreviewed health claims. No reel card is marked done from prose alone.
answers.stop_and_escalation_rules: Escalate to the owner before any Buffer schedule entry, before any TikTok publish, before using any new music or stock source, and whenever a draft might contain a food-safety or health claim. Stop the pipeline when the daily reel target is reached, when the ready-reel backlog falls below the configured minimum and no themes are approved, when TikTok Analytics or Buffer proof is unavailable, and when a theme's 48-hour engagement falls materially below the cut threshold for two consecutive reels.
